name: Auto-granted exact alarms
plain: Auto-granted exact alarm access for alarm and calendar apps.
meaning: Same capability as the exact alarm grant but granted at install and not user-revocable. Play restricts it to alarm and calendar apps.

android.store_policy: Play: restricted to alarm clock and calendar apps; declaration required

ios.note: AlarmKit in iOS 26 is the nearest equivalent.

limits.headline: Can set exact alarms by itself on Android, if it is an alarm or calendar app
limits.user_action: Nothing. Alarm and calendar apps get this when you install them
can: Fire alarms at exact times without a switch in Settings
Run alarm clock features and calendar reminders on time
cannot: Be turned off by you; Android auto grants it and you cannot revoke it
Be used by other kinds of apps in Google Play without review
Match this on iPhone, where AlarmKit in iOS 26 is the closest tool
limits.differs: Android grants this at install for alarm and calendar apps. iPhone's nearest tool is AlarmKit in iOS 26.

story.what_it_is: Exact alarm power handed out at install to alarm and calendar apps, and you cannot turn it off.

marketing.name: Exact alarms
marketing.pitch: Google describes a special permission that alarm and calendar apps get automatically for precise timing.

story.for_you: You do nothing and your alarm clock always rings on time. You also cannot take the power away.
story.for_makers: Alarm and calendar makers need it so alarms never fail. Google Play lets only those types use it.

use_cases.example: An alarm clock app that must always wake you.
A calendar app that rings every meeting on time.
A pill reminder that treats a missed alarm as a safety issue.
A study app with a fixed daily session alarm.
A workout planner that rings at the start of a class.
A flight app that rings before boarding.
A game claiming to be an alarm app to get exact timing, which Play does not allow.

risks: Abuse by apps that do not qualify
story.android_note: Granted at install. You cannot revoke it.
story.ios_note: iOS 26 adds AlarmKit as the nearest match.
